root_cause.text: In `net/mptcp/pm.c`’s ADD_ADDR retransmission timer handler, early `return` paths bypassed the final `sock_put()`/`__sock_put()` release after `sk_reset_timer()` had taken a socket reference, causing a refcount leak in the MPTCP path manager.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says “When an ADD_ADDR is retransmitted, the sk is held in sk_reset_timer(). It should then be released in all cases at the end” and notes that “Some (unlikely) checks were returning directly instead of calling sock_put()”; the patch fixes this by replacing the direct `return` on `inet_sk_state_load(sk) == TCP_CLOSE` with `goto exit` so `__sock_put(sk)` is always executed, and it removes an unreachable `!msk` early return.

It should then be released in all cases at the end” and notes that “Some (unlikely) checks were returning directly instead of calling sock_put()”; the patch fixes this by replacing the direct `return` on `inet_sk_state_load(sk) == TCP_CLOSE` with `goto exit` so `__sock_put(sk)` is always executed, and it removes an unreachable `!msk` early return.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adjust the timer callback to use the common exit path for closed sockets and remove the redundant null-pointer early return.
intent_record.what: In mptcp_pm_add_timer(), the code that returned early when `msk` was null was removed, and the TCP close-state check was changed from a standalone `if` return to an `unlikely()`-wrapped check that jumps to the existing `exit` label.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now only explicitly bails out when the socket state is `TCP_CLOSE`, using the shared exit path instead of an immediate return. This changes the control flow slightly but preserves the close-state guard, while no longer short-circuiting on a null `msk` at this point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a common exit label before socket release in the MPTCP timer handler to support correct cleanup across multiple paths.
intent_record.what: A new label `exit:` was inserted immediately before the `__sock_put(sk);` call at the end of `mptcp_pm_add_timer(struct timer_list *timer)`, following `bh_unlock_sock(sk);`.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter the normal execution path by itself, but it creates an additional jump target so control flow can be directed to the common socket release code from multiple exit paths, ensuring `__sock_put(sk)` is reached consistently when needed.

grouping_result.intent: Add a common exit label before socket release in the MPTCP timer handler to support correct cleanup across multiple paths.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make the MPTCP timer handler use a shared exit path before socket release so cleanup is handled consistently across paths.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: the MPTCP ADD_ADDR timer handler had early returns that skipped the final socket release after a timer-acquired reference. Introducing a shared exit path before socket release and removing an early return addresses that refcount leak.

candidates.rationale: This early null-check return can bypass the later shared cleanup path after the timer callback has taken a socket reference, contributing to the refcount leak described in the root cause.
This early return is one of the paths that exits before the final socket release, leaving the reference acquired by sk_reset_timer() unreleased.
This closed-socket check leads to an early return that skips the cleanup/release logic, matching the bug mechanism in the timer handler.
This second early return after the TCP_CLOSE check also bypasses the eventual sock_put/__sock_put() release, causing the leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This null-check gates an early exit in the timer handler; because the callback had already taken a socket reference via sk_reset_timer(), returning here skips the later sock_put()/__sock_put() cleanup and leaks the reference.
This early return is the concrete bypass of the cleanup path after the timer callback has acquired a socket reference, directly causing the refcount leak.
This closed-socket check introduces another early-exit path in the ADD_ADDR retransmission timer handler, skipping the final socket release and leaving the reference held.
This return after the TCP_CLOSE check bypasses the shared exit/cleanup path, so the socket reference acquired by sk_reset_timer() is not released.
